bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar : Agri dept to provide free sugarcane seeds to farmers under expansion scheme
bihar_raw_news.content: All News English Indian Sugar News Sugar News Muzaffarpur: The Bihar Agriculture Department will provide free sugarcane seed to farmers to encourage expansion of sugarcane cultivation across the state. Under the Sugarcane Expansion Scheme, farmers will be supported for cultivation across 200 acres, with applications to be submitted online, Jagran reported. Farmers cultivating up to one hectare will be eligible to receive the seed free of cost. The initiative is aimed at increasing the area under sugarcane cultivation and improving farm incomes. Assistant Sugarcane Director Arvind Kumar Ravi said a special campaign would be conducted across all 16 blocks of Muzaffarpur district to promote sugarcane planting. Farmers from each block can apply online to avail themselves of the scheme. The government will also provide subsidies to farmers for purchasing fertilizers and pesticides as part of the initiative. The department plans to promote sugarcane cultivation through greater access to quality planting material and cultivation support. Ravi said farmers could adopt two methods of sugarcane cultivation. In the first method, cane stalks are cut and planted directly in the field, requiring around 25 quintals of seed per acre. The second method involves planting nursery-raised seedlings, with around 10,000 plants required per acre. Sugarcane planting is generally undertaken in October and February. Once the crop is established from the initial planting material, farmers can obtain two additional crops through ratooning with the application of fertilizers and other inputs, according to the department. Under the scheme, farmers will be able to obtain planting material from designated nurseries. The department will directly pay the cost of the seed to the nursery operators. Ravi said sugarcane cultivation could provide significant returns to farmers. According to the department, an acre can produce around 300–400 quintals of sugarcane, potentially generating a profit of around ₹1 lakh to ₹1.5 lakh after cultivation costs. The department said it would continue implementing schemes to promote sugarcane cultivation and support higher farm incomes in Bihar.

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Floats Solar Dryer Plan, Seeks OEMs for Farm-Level Deployments - Saur Energy
bihar_raw_news.content: News Bihar Floats Solar Dryer Plan, Seeks OEMs for Farm-Level Deployments The smallest 20/25-kg package is aimed at individual farmers, kitchen gardens and small medicinal or aromatic plant growers, with portable cabinet. Manish Kumar 18 Sep 2026 09:48 IST Follow Us Bihar Floats Solar Dryer Plan, Seeks OEMs for Farm-Level Deployments Photograph: (AI) The Bihar Horticulture Development Society has invited bids from OEMs and authorised agencies for the supply, installation and maintenance of solar crop dryers across multiple capacity categories, ranging from 20 kg to 1,000 kg per batch. Advertisment The Bihar Horticulture Development Society (BHDS), under the state’s Department of Agriculture, has floated a request for proposal (RFP) to empanel Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) and OEM-authorised agencies for the supply, installation, commissioning, training, warranty support and maintenance of solar crop dryers across Bihar. Advertisment The procurement covers solar crop dryers with capacities of 20/25 kg, 50 kg, 100 kg, 250 kg, 500 kg and a special 1,000-kg category, according to the RFP. The dryers are intended to support farmers and horticulture-related users in drying agricultural and horticultural produce. The tender has been floated through the Bihar government's e-procurement portal. The last date for submission of bids is October 8, 2026, at 3 pm, while technical bids are scheduled to open the same day at 3:30 pm. A pre-bid meeting is scheduled for September 24 at 1:15 pm in hybrid/online mode. The date for financial bid opening will be communicated to technically qualified bidders. Advertisment Six capacity categories The RFP has divided the solar crop dryers into different capacity packages based on their intended users. The smallest 20/25-kg package is aimed at individual farmers, kitchen gardens and small medicinal or aromatic plant growers, with portable cabinet, box or foldable configurations envisaged. The 50-kg category is intended for progressive farmers, small self-help groups (SHGs), nurseries and demonstration centres, while the 100-kg category targets SHGs, Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs), village enterprises and common facility centres. Advertisment The larger 250-kg package is designed for FPOs, farmer clusters and institutional buyers, while the 500-kg category targets large FPOs, aggregation centres and processing clusters. A special 1,000-kg category is reserved for cluster or institutional projects and can be deployed only after site feasibility, civil-space confirmation, power/backup planning and separate approval by BHDS. Advertisment Solar-powered drying system The tender defines a solar crop dryer as a protected drying system using solar thermal energy and/or solar PV-powered air circulation/control, with an optional hybrid backup, for controlled drying of agricultural and horticultural produce. The minimum technical specifications require an indirect solar crop dryer with forced convection. The systems are expected to handle fruits, vegetables, spices, medicinal and aromatic plants, grains and other agricultural or horticultural products. The dryers will have to use SS 304 food-grade trays and food-contact surfaces, while the drying temperature range is specified at 40°C to 70°C. Air circulation is to be achieved through solar-powered DC fans or blowers, with protection against bird and animal intrusion. national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi today stated that India is taking every step needed to become a preferred destination for the semiconductor industry. Inaugurating SEMICON India 2026 at Yashobhoomi in New Delhi today, Mr Modi said the world is looking for new and trusted manufacturing destinations and India is steadily preparing itself to meet this need. Mr Modi highlighted that India’s semiconductor ecosystem is expanding rapidly and opening new opportunities for innovation, investment and growth.. He discussed how the explosive demand for Artificial Intelligence is shifting the focus from mere transistor size to holistic system integration, including memory placement and heat management. Mr Modi said that on one side India’s economy is growing and the other side, global trust in India is also growing. He said, despite the challenging global environment, India recorded a growth rate of 7.8 per cent. Prime Minister said, at the same time, Japan’s credit rating agency also upgraded India’s sovereign rating. Mr Modi said, every citizen of the country is working with a commitment to build a developed India. Prime Minister said, India’s semiconductor ecosystem is expanding rapidly and it is is opening new opportunities for innovation, investment and growth. Prime Minister Modi said, India Semiconductor Mission 2.0 expanded outlay to 13.5 billion US dollar from eight billion US dollar in the first phase. He highlighted that so far 12 chip making projects have been approved in the next phase it will further increase. In his address, the Prime Minister also mentioned about recently held BRICS Summit in New Delhi. He said, India successfully hosted the summit in which New Delhi Declaration was adopted with consensus of every member country. Mr Modi said, it is another major testament to the world’s trust in India. He said, young talents who are researching in India should come forward. Mr Modi said, the youth who are researching abroad should also join the development of advanced technologies in India. He urged industry leaders to spearhead Research and Development in the country. He added that this will be mutually beneficial, driving industry growth while empowering India’s youth. On the occasion, Union Minister of Electronics and IT Ashwini Vaishnaw said that India had wanted to establish a semiconductor industry for several decades, but it was possible only under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. He said, the foundation has now been laid and the next step is to build the industry through Semicon 2.0, which focuses on six major pillars. This include semiconductor design, machines and materials, memory, silicon, compound and logic fabrication units and research and development. He said, the government has set a target to support at least 200 startups and companies to design chips in India across the spectrum of semiconductor requirements. Minister of State for Electronics and IT Jitin Prasada, Secretary S Krishnan, officials, delegations were present on the occasion. The SEMICON India 2026 event has brought together over 600 exhibitors, 300 international companies, and delegations from more than 50 countries. The exhibition features six country pavilions representing Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Netherlands, Singapore and Sweden, twelve State Government pavilions, and a dedicated Startup Pavilion.The conference and exhibition, being held from today is being organised on the theme Silicon to Systems: Building the Ecosystem. It has brought together global and Indian companies, policymakers, investors, researchers, start-ups, academic institutions and students from across the semiconductor and electronics value chain.

national_raw_news.title: PM Vishwakarma completes three years with 30 lakh artisans registered under the scheme
national_raw_news.content: PM Vishwakarma completes three years with 30 lakh artisans registered under the scheme Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर PM Vishwakarma completes three years with 30 lakh artisans registered under the scheme ANI | Updated: Sep 18, 2026 06:18 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], September 18 (ANI): The Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (MSME) celebrated the 3rd Anniversary of the PM Vishwakarma Scheme at Dhono Dhanyo Auditorium, Kolkata, West Bengal, on Thursday. According to a release from the Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises, the occasion marked three years of the Scheme’s implementation and highlighted the Government’s continued efforts to strengthen the livelihoods, skills and entrepreneurial capabilities of traditional artisans and craftspeople. West Bengal onboarded for the implementation of PM Vishwakarma in May, marking an important step towards extending comprehensive support to the State’s traditional artisans and craftspeople. The celebrations in Kolkata underscored the scheme’s significance in empowering Vishwakarmas through skill training, modern tools, institutional credit and market linkages. On the occasion of the 3rd Anniversary of PM Vishwakarma, an exhibition showcasing the rich traditional arts and crafts of Vishwakarma artisans was inaugurated by Jitan Ram Manjhi, Union Cabinet Minister, Ministry of MSME, Sushri Shobha Karandlaje, Union Minister of State for MSME, Dipak Barman, Minister of MSME & Textiles, Government of West Bengal and Ashoke Dinda, Minister of State for MSME & Textiles, Government of West Bengal. The exhibition provided Vishwakarmas of West Bengal, a platform to showcase their traditional craftsmanship and entrepreneurial skills. Addressing the gathering, West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari highlighted the importance of extending skill training and credit support to traditional artisans and craftspeople in the state. He expressed his gratitude to Prime Minister Narendra Modi for the transformative vision behind PM Vishwakarma and acknowledged its significant role in strengthening the livelihood of artisans and craftspeople across the country. Outlining the progress of PM Vishwakarma in West Bengal, he stated that more than 7 lakh applications have been received under the scheme. He stated that the Government of West Bengal will expedite the provision of facilitative support to enable Vishwakarmas to avail the benefits under the scheme. The Chief Minister also assured coordinated efforts by the State for effective and timely implementation of PM Vishwakarma across West Bengal in association with the Ministry of MSME, Government of India. He called upon the concerned State agencies to strengthen outreach and implementation so that the benefits of the scheme reach every eligible artisan and craftsperson. He appreciated the implementation of various schemes and initiatives of the Ministry of MSME in West Bengal, noting their contribution to promoting entrepreneurship, generating employment, supporting enterprise development and strengthening the MSME ecosystem in the State. He emphasised that effective implementation of these initiatives would contribute towards realising PM Modi’s vision of a Viksit Bharat.
